In [[mathematics]], the '''Neuman–Sándor mean''' of two positive, unequal numbers <math>a</math> and <math>b</math> is defined as

:<math>
M(a,b) = \frac{a-b} {2\operatorname{arcsinh}\left(\frac{a-b} {a+b}\right)}.
</math>

This mean <math>M</math> satisfies the inequality <math>A<M<T</math>, where <math>A</math> is the unweighted arithmetic mean <math>A=(a+b)/2</math> and <math>T</math> is the second Seiffert mean

: <math>
T(a,b)=\frac{a-b} {2\arctan\left(\frac{a-b} {a+b}\right)}.
</math>

The ''M''(''a'',''b'') mean, introduced by [[Edward Neuman]] and József Sándor,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Neuman |first1=E. |author1-link=Edward Neuman |last2=Sándor |first2=J. |title=On the Schwab–Borchardt mean |journal=Mathematica Pannonica |volume=14 |issue=2 |year=2003 |pages=253–266 |zbl=1053.26015}}</ref> has recently been the subject of intensive research and many remarkable inequalities for this mean can be found in the literature.<ref>Tiehong Zhao, Yuming Chu and Baoyu Liu. Some Best Possible Inequalities Concerning Certain Bivariate Means. October 15, 2012. {{ArXiv|1210.4219}}</ref> Several authors obtained sharp and optimal bounds for the Neuman–Sándor mean.<ref>Wei-Dong Jiang & Feng Qi. Sharp bounds for the Neuman-Sándor mean in terms of the power and contraharmonic means. January 9, 2015. https://www.cogentoa.com/article/10.1080/23311835.2014.995951</ref><ref>Hui Sun, Tiehong Zhao, Yuming Chu and Baoyu Liu. A note on the Neuman-Sándor mean. ''J. of Math. Inequal.'' dx.doi.org/10.7153/jmi-08-20</ref><ref>Huang, HY., Wang, N. & Long, BY. Optimal bounds for Neuman–Sándor mean in terms of the geometric convex combination of two Seiffert means. ''J Inequal Appl'' (2016) 2016: 14. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13660-015-0955-2</ref><ref>Chu, YM., Long, BY., Gong, WM. et al. Sharp bounds for Seiffert and Neuman-Sándor means in terms of generalized logarithmic means. ''J Inequal Appl'' (2013) 2013: 10. https://doi.org/10.1186/1029-242X-2013-10</ref><ref>Tie-Hong Zhao, Yu-Ming Chu, and Bao-Yu Liu, “Optimal Bounds for Neuman-Sándor Mean in Terms of the Convex Combinations of Harmonic, Geometric, Quadratic, and Contraharmonic Means,” Abstract and Applied Analysis, vol. 2012, Article ID 302635, 9 pages, 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/302635</ref> Neuman and others utilized this mean to study other bivariate means and inequalities.<ref>E. Neuman, Inequalities for weighted sums of powers and their applications, ''Math. Inequal. Appl.'' 15 (2012), No. 4, 995–1005.</ref><ref>E. Neuman, A note on a certain bivariate mean, ''J. Math. Inequal.'' 6 (2012), No. 4, 637–643</ref><ref>Y.-M. Li, B.-Y. Long and Y.-M. Chu.

Inequal.'' 7 (2013), No. 3, 399–412</ref><ref>E. Neuman, Sharp inequalities involving Neuman–Sándor and logarithmic means, ''J. Math. Inequal.'' 7 (2013), No. 3, 413–419</ref>
